### 9. Building a graph from an SCM

Consider the SCM

$$
\begin{aligned}
W&\leftarrow f_W(\epsilon_W),\\
X&\leftarrow f_X(\epsilon_X),\\
A&\leftarrow f_A(W,X,\epsilon_A),\\
M&\leftarrow f_M(W,A,\epsilon_M),\\
Y&\leftarrow f_Y(X,M,\epsilon_Y),
\end{aligned}
$$

where the noise terms are independent.

a. Draw the causal graph.

b. List the parents of every variable.

<div class="response-space"></div>

::: {.answer-block}
**Solution**

**a.** The causal graph is

![](images/02c-exercise-scm-graph.svg){width=680 fig-align="center" fig-alt="W and X point to A. W and A point to M. X and M point to Y."}

**b.** The parent sets are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Pa}_W&=\varnothing,\\
\operatorname{Pa}_X&=\varnothing,\\
\operatorname{Pa}_A&=\{W,X\},\\
\operatorname{Pa}_M&=\{W,A\},\\
\operatorname{Pa}_Y&=\{X,M\}.
\end{aligned}
$$
:::

### 10. Recovering an SCM from a graph

Consider the following causal graph.

![](images/02c-exercise-graph-to-scm.svg){width=500 fig-align="center" fig-alt="W and X point to A. W and A point to Y."}

a. List the parents of every variable.

b. Write the SCM represented by the graph.

c. State what must be true of the noise terms.

<div class="response-space"></div>

::: {.answer-block}
**Solution**

**a.** The parent sets are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Pa}_W&=\varnothing,\\
\operatorname{Pa}_X&=\varnothing,\\
\operatorname{Pa}_A&=\{W,X\},\\
\operatorname{Pa}_Y&=\{W,A\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

**b.** The graph represents the SCM

$$
\begin{aligned}
W&\leftarrow f_W(\epsilon_W),\\
X&\leftarrow f_X(\epsilon_X),\\
A&\leftarrow f_A(W,X,\epsilon_A),\\
Y&\leftarrow f_Y(W,A,\epsilon_Y).
\end{aligned}
$$

**c.** The noise terms $\epsilon_W$, $\epsilon_X$, $\epsilon_A$, and $\epsilon_Y$ must be mutually independent.
:::

### 11. Cycles and topological orders

For each graph, determine whether the corresponding SCM has a topological order. If it does, give one. If it does not, identify a directed cycle.

![](images/02c-exercise-cycle-panels.svg){width=850 fig-align="center" fig-alt="Three graphs. In graph a, A and B point to C, which points to D. In graph b, A points to B, B points to C, C points back to A, and C points to D. In graph c, X points to M and Y, and M points to Y."}

<div class="response-space"></div>

::: {.answer-block}
**Solution**

**a.** The corresponding SCM has a topological order. One is

$$
A,B,C,D.
$$

The order $B,A,C,D$ also works.

**b.** The corresponding SCM does not have a topological order. The graph contains the directed cycle

$$
A\to B\to C\to A.
$$

**c.** The corresponding SCM has the topological order

$$
X,M,Y.
$$
:::

### 12. Using the graph for conditional independence

Return to the graph from Exercise 9 and use the topological order

$$
W,X,A,M,Y.
$$

a. For each variable, identify the variables that appear earlier in the order but are not its parents.

b. Use the local Markov property to list every nontrivial conditional-independence statement supplied by this order.

c. Does the local Markov property tell us whether $A$ and $X$ are dependent? Does it tell us whether $Y$ and $W$ are conditionally dependent given $X$? Explain.

<div class="response-space"></div>

::: {.answer-block}
**Solution**

**a.** There are no earlier variables when we reach $W$. When we reach $X$, the earlier variable $W$ is not a parent. The parents of $A$ are both earlier variables, $W$ and $X$. When we reach $M$, the earlier variable $X$ is not a parent. When we reach $Y$, the earlier variables $W$ and $A$ are not parents.

**b.** The nontrivial conditional-independence statements are

$$
X\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}W,
$$

$$
M\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X\mid W,A,
$$

and

$$
Y\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}(W,A)\mid X,M.
$$

**c.** No in both cases. The local Markov property tells us when the SCM guarantees an independence or conditional independence. It does not guarantee dependence when it supplies no independence statement.

Because $X$ is a parent of $A$, the property does not give $A\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}X$, but that does not prove that $A$ and $X$ are dependent. Likewise, the property does not give $Y\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}W\mid X$, but that does not establish that $Y$ and $W$ are conditionally dependent given $X$. Whether dependence occurs can depend on the assignment functions and noise distributions.
:::
